summary: A risk-off day across crypto driven almost entirely by macro, not coin-specific news. Bitcoin held below $80K (~5% under the prior week's high) as traders de-risked ahead of Friday's August CPI — the last inflation print before the Fed's Sep 15-16 meeting — while rising Treasury yields and Middle East tensions weighed on risk assets broadly. US spot Bitcoin ETFs extended outflows for a third straight session. The altcoin futures moves flagged in this report were low-cap and idiosyncratic; no confirmed mainstream or social-media catalyst was found for the individual names, so they are described from price data alone.

items.headline: Bitcoin holds below $80K, ~5% under last week's high, as risk appetite fades
items.note: BTC traded near $77-78K with total crypto market cap around $2.76T. Renewed Middle East tensions and rising US Treasury yields pressured risk assets generally, dragging altcoins with it.

items.headline: US spot Bitcoin ETFs post a third straight day of outflows (~$449M over 3 sessions)
items.note: Roughly $282.7M left spot BTC ETFs on Sep 10 alone, with ARKB accounting for over half. Read as pre-CPI profit-taking rather than a trend change. (A separate tally put the single-day net nearer $120M — figures vary by data provider.)

items.headline: Markets de-risk ahead of August CPI, the last inflation print before the Fed meeting
items.note: CPI was due Friday Sep 11, immediately before the Fed's Sep 15-16 decision. It later printed +0.4% m/m and +3.4% y/y (core +0.3% / +2.4%), keeping rate-cut hopes in question. Fear & Greed index sat at 69 (Greed) despite the pullback.

items.headline: ECB raises its policy rate to 2.50% from 2.25%
items.note: The ECB's second hike of the year, aimed at energy-driven inflation tied to the Middle East conflict. Tighter global liquidity is a mild headwind for risk assets including crypto.
